ev.q: CDC analyzed 2008–2017 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) data to examine trends
In 2017, only one in four (25.3%) urban residents and one in five (19.6%) rural residents met the combined guidelines.
Among urban residents, the prevalence was higher during 2016–2017 than during 2008–2009
In 2017, only one in four (25.3%) urban residents
Among rural residents, the prevalence increased across all demographic and regional subgroups except Hispanics
prevalence of meeting the combined guidelines was estimated separately for urban and rural residents, stratified by demographic characteristics and region
NHIS is an annual, multistage probability sample of U.S. households
From 2008 to 2017, the age-standardized prevalence of meeting the combined physical activity guidelines increased 30.4%

methods_quotes.q: Trends were assessed using age-adjusted logistic regression and orthogonal polynomial contrasts
the best-fitting model was identified using sequential permutation tests in JoinPoint
Differences between periods were tested using adjusted Wald tests
Weighted analyses were performed in Stata (version 15; StataCorp) following NHIS analytic guidelines
Estimates were age-adjusted using the 2000 U.S. population as the standard population
